title: Successor maps independent modulo preceding filtration stages have an injective sum
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $X$ an $R$-module, $\kappa$ a set ordinal, and $(X_\beta)_{\beta\leq\kappa}$ an increasing family of $R$-submodules of $X$. For each $\alpha<\kappa$ let $A_\alpha$ be an $R$-module and $t_\alpha:A_\alpha\to X_{\alpha+1}$ an $R$-linear map. Put $D=\bigoplus_{\alpha<\kappa}A_\alpha$ using [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], and let $f:D\to X$ be the $R$-linear map $f((a_\alpha))=\sum_{\alpha\in\operatorname{supp}(a)}t_\alpha(a_\alpha)$, with each value included in $X$. Assume for every $\alpha<\kappa$ and $a\in A_\alpha$ that $t_\alpha(a)\in X_\alpha$ implies $a=0$. Then $f$ is injective: for every finitely supported family $(a_\alpha)$, the equality $\sum_\alpha t_\alpha(a_\alpha)=0$ implies $a_\alpha=0$ for all $\alpha<\kappa$. This assertion does not require $X_0=0$, exhaustion $X_\kappa=X$, continuity at limit stages, or generation of the successor stages.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, proof lines 20435–20453: injectivity from independence of each new summand from its predecessor; equivalent maximal finite-support formulation, for arbitrary maps injective modulo the preceding stage.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], an element $a$ of $D$ has finite support $S=\{\alpha<\kappa:a_\alpha\ne0\}$. The displayed sum defining $f$ is linear: for addition sum over the finite union of the two supports and use additivity of every $t_\alpha$; for scalar multiplication use the same finite support and $t_\alpha(ra_\alpha)=rt_\alpha(a_\alpha)$, allowing zero terms.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, injectivity paragraph, lines 20435–20453; finite-support reformulation.

proof.text: Let $f(a)=0$. If $S$ is empty then all coordinates vanish. Otherwise a nonempty finite set in a linear order has a largest element: for a singleton take its element, and on adjoining one element replace the old largest element by the larger of the two. Apply this finite-set induction to the ordinal order to obtain $\gamma=\max S<\kappa$, with $a_\gamma\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, injectivity paragraph, lines 20435–20453; finite-support reformulation.

proof.text: For every $\alpha\in S\setminus\{\gamma\}$, maximality gives $\alpha<\gamma$, hence $\alpha+1\le\gamma$. Since the filtration is increasing, $t_\alpha(a_\alpha)\in X_{\alpha+1}\subseteq X_\gamma$. Closure of the submodule $X_\gamma$ under addition (induct on the finite number of terms) and negation therefore gives $-\sum_{\alpha\in S\setminus\{\gamma\}}t_\alpha(a_\alpha)\in X_\gamma$.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, injectivity paragraph, lines 20435–20453; finite-support reformulation.

proof.text: Separating the $\gamma$ term in $f(a)=0$ gives $t_\gamma(a_\gamma)=-\sum_{\alpha\in S\setminus\{\gamma\}}t_\alpha(a_\alpha)\in X_\gamma$. The assumed implication for $t_\gamma$ forces $a_\gamma=0$, contradicting $\gamma\in S$. Thus $S$ must be empty, so every coordinate of every element sent to zero is zero.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, injectivity paragraph, lines 20435–20453; finite-support reformulation.

proof.text: If $f(a)=f(b)$, linearity gives $f(a-b)=0$. The preceding steps give $a_\alpha-b_\alpha=0$ for every $\alpha$, hence $a=b$ as families. Thus $f$ is injective. If $\kappa=0$ there are no coordinates and the same argument applies. Only monotonicity, finite support and the stated successor implication were used; the four additional conditions excluded in the statement are unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, injectivity paragraph, lines 20435–20453; finite-support reformulation.
